title: kumihan conformance case file
description: One file per JLReq section. The format is specified by docs/design/conformance.md and enforced by `cargo run -p xtask -- conform --check`; the two are one contract stated twice, once for this workspace and once for everyone else. Every number is an integer inside 2^53, so a parser using IEEE-754 doubles is exact (ADR 0005). Every amount is written as a fraction and a unit count that agree under the current denominator, so the published suite is independent of kumihan's 1/720 unit (ADR 0007).

$schema.description: Points at the committed schema beside the cases directory.

section.description: The JLReq section this file is about, in the canonical address rendering. It is also the file's own name.

heading_en.description: The section heading, quoted from the published document. JLReq publishes every heading in two locales, so a file carrying one carries the other.

cases.description: The cases this section publishes, each with a unique id.

address.description: A rule address in the specification's own spelling: a section path, a section and a note ordinal, or one matrix cell. One rendering is canonical and nothing else is an address, so the bytes in a generated table, in a doc comment and in a case file are the same bytes (ADR 0013). `#` separates a note ordinal, which the published document gives no machine-readable identifier; `line-head` and `line-end` are the two axes the matrices print as prose labels. A matrix carries one line-head row and one line-end column, so the two are not interchangeable.

matrix_cell.description: One coordinate of one captured matrix (Table 1 through 6), named the way `spec/captured/table<N>.<locale>.tsv` and `xtask::attest` key it — a table number and the two axis labels as the published table prints them — rather than through `address`'s own `@` suffix. That grammar names one cell only when its section prefix names exactly one table, and an appendix's own legend section does not always: §D.1 is the legend of *three* matrices (its own heading is "Legend of Tables 3, 4 and 5"), so `D.1@cl-02,line-end` never named one cell to begin with, and `spec/derived/rules.tsv` does not even inventory the natural per-table alternative — it has `B`, `C`, `C.3`, `D`, `D.1` and `E`, never `B.1`, `C.1` or `E.1`. `table`/`before`/`after` sidesteps the ambiguity by naming the table directly, in the identical three columns the transcription itself is keyed on.

table.description: Which of the six matrices this coordinate is in.

before.description: The row label, as the matrix prints it: a character class, or `line-head`. `line-head` is a row of Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 alone (§C.1, §E.1).

after.description: The column label, as the matrix prints it: a character class, or `line-end`. `line-end` is a column of Tables 1, 3, 4 and 5 alone (§C.1, §E.1).

integer.description: An integer a JSON parser using IEEE-754 doubles reads exactly.

fraction.description: An amount as JLReq states it: a numerator and a denominator, as a fraction of the referent's em. Not confined to Table 1's tokens, because §3.1.6 requires a full em after a sentence-final dividing punctuation mark.

amount.description: One amount, stated three ways that must agree: the fraction JLReq writes, the same amount in kumihan's 1/720 unit, and the same amount resolved into the case's own caller units. `conform --check` asserts the first two agree under the current denominator, which is what makes the published suite denominator-independent.

case.description: One case: one input, and what the specification permits and forbids as an answer to it.

rules.description: Every rule this case exercises, by address. The declared-coverage gate subtracts the union of these from the rule inventory and requires the remainder to be empty.

covers.description: A family: a row, a column or a class-pair set of one matrix, credited whole by the declared-coverage gate. Table cells are rules, so the inventory runs to several thousand and a case per cell would be abandoned; a family still has to exercise each cell it claims under the dynamic half of the gate.

cells.description: Every captured matrix coordinate this boundary case exercises, named unambiguously by table number rather than through the `address` grammar's own `@` suffix (see `matrix_cell`'s own description for why that grammar does not suffice here). Optional, and not a substitute for `rules` or `covers`: `xtask attest`'s `conformance-cases-agree-with-the-cells` invariant (ADR 0006) is this field's only reader, comparing the declared coordinate against `spec/captured/`'s own independently double-entered transcription — existence at every table, and, for Table 1 alone, whether the case's own default-policy (`policy: {}`) answer agrees with the captured amount. `conform`'s declared-coverage gate never reads it and no evaluator ever fires a bare cell address, which is why this is a field of its own rather than an entry in `rules`. A boundary case that omits it declares nothing about the transcription either way — the field exists so a case can state a coordinate its own words settle, not so every case must.

standing.description: What kind of claim this case makes, matching `jlreq_spec::Standing`. `unstated` and `adjudicated` record that JLReq does not decide, and both readings then appear under `permitted` with `source` naming each. Nothing in this format lets a silence be laundered into a requirement.

quote.description: The specification sentence, verbatim, so a report is readable without kumihan's source. A field rather than a comment, because JSON has none and because a published disagreement must appear in a report.

rationale.description: Why the expectations below follow from that sentence, in a sentence a reviewer can disagree with.

permitted.description: The (policy, expectation) pairs the specification permits. A `policy` is an overlay on `Policy::JLREQ`, not an identity; the entry that applies to a declared policy and names the most questions is the one selected, and `conform --check` makes that unique by requiring the entries' key sets to be totally ordered by inclusion.

forbidden.description: Outcomes the specification excludes even though they lie between two permitted ones. §3.1.9's quarter em is the canonical instance, and it is the value a naively continuous justifier emits.

disagreements.description: Implementations kumihan has measured that answer this case differently, with kumihan's own reading and the evidence for it. Data rather than prose, so a disagreement appears in a report (ADR 0006).

input.description: What the case supplies: the base running-text stream, any annotation streams, the constructs over them, the break opportunities, and the measure. Exactly what `Paragraph` accepts and nothing else — whether a line is the last one, for instance, is something composition decides.

kind.description: Which of the eight questions this case asks. A `compose` case additionally requires `candidates` and `measure`, because a line cannot be composed without them. An `align` case additionally requires `measure` and `alignment`, because `jlreq_line::align` needs a target and a method; it takes no `candidates`, because it never breaks. A `tab` case is the asymmetric one: it needs neither `candidates` nor `measure` at all — `jlreq_line::tab_line` places every target run against its own caller-declared tab stops, never against a caller-stated line length — and instead requires `tab_starts` and `tab_stops`, the vocabulary §3.6.1 itself names (tab positions, tab types, and where each target string begins). A `feasible` case is the sixth and asks a different layer's question entirely: not Table 1's and Table 2's own class-pair verdict at one adjacency (that is `boundary`), but which of the caller's own UAX #14 break candidates `jlreq_line::Feasible::compute` leaves standing once kinsoku has been applied — the layer ADR 0003 states may only remove an opportunity a caller offered, never add one — and, for each one it refuses, which rule refused it. It additionally requires `candidates`, the field `compose` also reads, but reads no `measure`: kinsoku's own refusal has no line length to compose against. It is one of three kinds for which `constructs` is not merely optional but load-bearing (`$defs/constructs`'s own description states which): `feasible` is answered by converting `constructs` into a real `jlreq_unit::Runs` and handing it to `Feasible::compute` directly, which is what makes §C.2 notes 6 through 8 and 13's same-run refusal — a fact no table cell can express, because a class pair alone does not say whether two occurrences share one construct run — reachable by a case at all. A `lower` case is the seventh, and asks a third layer's question again: not the line layer at all, but the inline-construct layer directly beneath it — what `jlreq_inline::lower` computes from a caller-declared `Constructs` and hands across the seam. `constructs` is this kind's own subject in full, not merely load-bearing beside other fields: a `lower` case declares one or more `ruby` constructs (the only kind `jlreq_inline::Constructs` accepts a builder for today) and asks what `lower` resolved for one of them — its run identity against its neighbors, the forced boundary spacing §3.3.8 rule 1 computes, and, for `RubyStyle::MonoRuby` and `RubyStyle::JukugoRuby` alike, which `RubyAlignment` §3.3.5 resolved (§3.3.7¶1 delegates a jukugo compound's own ≤2-character runs to that identical method, so `lower` resolves the identical fact for it) and whether it is the discouraged combination. It requires `constructs` and reads no `measure`, no `candidates`, no `alignment`, no `tab_starts` and no `tab_stops`: `lower` never composes a line and never breaks one, so none of those fields is this kind's own question. A `place` case is the eighth, and asks the inline-construct layer's *positioning* question, downstream of `lower`'s own resolution rather than a restatement of it: not what `lower` resolved (that is `lower`), but what `jlreq_inline::place` computes for a caller-declared `Constructs` once the alignment `lower` resolved is read and consumed rather than re-derived — one `Attachment` per placed annotation character — mono-ruby's own, group-ruby's own and, as of M4-a round 7, a jukugo compound's own under either of §3.3.7's own two paragraphs — and every run `Attachments::declined` names, for one of four reasons: every mono-ruby run, or jukugo paragraph-1 run routed through the identical method, whose own §3.3.5(c) katatsuki-with-overflow choice is left unresolved; every group-ruby run, or jukugo paragraph-2 compound answering `Question::JUKUGO_RUBY_LAYOUT`'s own `group` (`decision:jukugo-group-layout-distribution`), whose ruby is genuinely longer than its base, §3.3.6 paragraph 3's own half neither of whose two stated methods `jlreq_inline::place` can perform; every jukugo compound answering `phonetic`, §F's own distribution being unimplemented; and every jukugo compound whose base range one `place` call's own line only partially covers. It requires `constructs`, the identical subject `lower` is answered over, and reads no `measure`, no `candidates`, no `alignment`, no `tab_starts` and no `tab_stops`, for the identical reason `lower` reads none of them. The line layout `place` positions each attachment against — the `items`/`placements` pair `jlreq_line::Line` would ordinarily supply — is not a field this format states at all: it is *derived* from the case's own declared item advances, plus every forced boundary separation §3.3.8 rule 1 computes for the declared constructs, rather than accepted as a further caller-declared array. A caller-declared `placements` array could assert a relationship between two numbers the case itself invented, with nothing in the format able to catch a caller who let the two disagree — the 'measuring nothing' failure this project's own §D.2#4 deferral prose forbids, and a subtler one than a stated scope limit, because it would look like a stronger assertion than it is. `crates/jlreq-conform/src/kumihan.rs`'s own `Compose::place` doc states the derivation in full and the Table 1 coordinates a multi-item fixture must independently verify blank for it to be trustworthy. `measure`, `alignment`, `tab_starts`, `tab_stops`, `search`, `first_line_indent`, `head_indent`, `end_indent` and `widow_threshold` are all ignored for `feasible`, `lower` and `place` alike, the same reading `alignment` already gets from a `classify` or `boundary` case. A value outside this enum is refused by the reader rather than defaulted: a runner that treated an unrecognized kind as a composition question would ask a case a question it did not ask, and this contract could not express that.

text.description: The base running-text stream, in reading order.

scales.description: The character sizes this stream declares, in the caller's own unit.

items.description: One item per occurrence, in reading order.

annotations.description: Further streams, each the same shape as the base one, because annotation text is a second stream and not a range of the first (ADR 0016). Indexed by `annotation` in `constructs`. The ruby size is stated here and only here: §3.3.3 does not close the set, and the caller shaped the reading at some size and measured it there.

candidates.description: The break opportunities the caller's UAX #14 implementation found. An offset of zero and an offset at the end of the text name the paragraph's own edges; both are accepted and neither creates a line (ADR 0018).

measure.description: The line length, in the caller's own unit.

search.description: Which of `jlreq_line::Search`'s two variants a `compose` case is measured under. Absent means `Search::FirstFit`, `jlreq-line`'s own greedy scan — the reading every case published before this field existed already assumed, so an implementation reads an absent `search` exactly as it always did and none of those cases' own expectations change. `kind: "optimal"` asks for `Search::Optimal` instead, over the same candidates and measure. Not a bare two-valued enum, because `Search::Optimal` itself is not one: it carries a `tolerance`, so a case naming it states one too. A `kind` this format does not recognize is refused by the reader rather than defaulted to either variant, the same discipline `kind` at the top of this object states for the eight questions themselves: defaulting an unrecognized search to `FirstFit` would measure a case against a narrower search than its own words asked for, and defaulting it to `Optimal` would ask the DP a question the case never posed. Ignored for any `kind` but `compose`, the same reading `alignment` gets from a `classify` or `boundary` case.

kind.description: `first-fit` names `jlreq_line::Search::FirstFit` explicitly — permitted, not refused, the same as naming `direction: "horizontal"` when horizontal is also what an absent field would read as. `optimal` names `jlreq_line::Search::Optimal` and requires `tolerance` alongside it, the same 'additionally requires' reading this object's own sibling `kind` field states for `measure` and `candidates` on a `compose` case: not enforced by this schema's own `required` array, because JSON Schema cannot express a requirement conditioned on a sibling's value without a duplicate `if`/`then` branch this format does not otherwise use, but enforced by the reader, on the same 'malformed case' standard `Kumihan::compose` already holds an absent `measure` to.

tolerance.description: The worst per-line `Badness` (`jlreq_line::Badness`, `0` to `10000`) `Search::Optimal` accepts without discarding a line before searching further — `jlreq_line::Search::Optimal`'s own field, required alongside `kind: "optimal"` and ignored for `kind: "first-fit"`, which reads no tolerance at all. `Search::Optimal`'s own doc states this milestone's zero-flex reading makes exactly two settings behaviorally distinct, not a spectrum: `10000` (`Badness::WORST`), the neutral, most permissive tolerance, which admits a ladder-exhausted line exactly as freely as `FirstFit` already does; and every value below it, which all read identically to `0`, because a line this milestone's ladder can fit always reports exactly `Badness::ZERO` and one it cannot always reports exactly `Badness::WORST` — nothing graduated is reachable yet for a value in between to buy a case. This field still accepts the full `0`-`10000` range `Badness::new` itself does, rather than a two-valued enum, because narrowing the published vocabulary to the two behaviors reachable today would have to widen again the day a later milestone's ladder reports a graduated residual, and a fact of this milestone's own ladder is not one to encode into the field `Search::Optimal` itself carries.

direction.description: The writing direction, when the case is specific to one. A case naming neither is composed both ways by the direction-parity gate and the inline results must be bit-identical, which is how ADR 0011's "exactly three direction-conditional rules" is proved over the whole corpus rather than reviewed.

first_line_indent.description: The paragraph's first-line indent, in the caller's own unit.

head_indent.description: The paragraph's line head indent, in the caller's own unit. Where `first_line_indent` applies once, to the paragraph's own first line, this narrows every line's own measure, first line included (the two add where both are stated).

end_indent.description: The paragraph's line end indent, in the caller's own unit, narrowing every line's own composition target from the line end side.

widow_threshold.description: §3.5.4's own "a given number of characters": the fewest items — not code points and not bytes, because nothing in this workspace counts by either (ADR 0008) — the paragraph's own last line must carry before `jlreq_line::compose` reports a `ViolationKind::Widow` against it (`docs/decisions/widow-threshold.md`'s own Q1, argued from that same absence of a code-point-granular counting anywhere else in this crate). Absent reads as `0`, `Paragraph::new`'s own default and the reading every one of the cases published before this field existed already assumed, so none of their own expectations change by this field's own arrival. A threshold of `0` is consequently a no-op by construction, `Paragraph::with_widow_threshold`'s own doc states, rather than a value this reader special-cases to skip. A value this reader cannot hold as a `u16` — negative, or past `65535` — is refused rather than silently clamped or defaulted, the same "malformed case" standard `search`'s own `kind` states for a value its own vocabulary does not carry. Bounded here to the same `0`-`65535` range `check_widow_threshold` enforces as a gate failure, the same 'declarative bound backs the prose' treatment `search.tolerance` gets above. Ignored for any `kind` but `compose`, the same reading `alignment` gets from a `classify` or `boundary` case.

alignment.description: Which of `jlreq_line::Alignment`'s four methods an `align` case asks for. Required for an `align` case, because `jlreq_line::align` takes one; merely ignored for any other kind, the same reading `first_line_indent` already gets from a `classify` or `boundary` case.

tab_starts.description: For a `tab` case: `starts[k]` is the item ordinal of the base stream where the run after the `k`-th tab sign begins, in the order the tab signs appear along the running text (§3.6.1's own 'the series of characters just after the tab sign are the target characters') — `jlreq_line::tab_line`'s own `starts` argument. Required of a `tab` case; absent or ignored for any other kind.

tab_stops.description: For a `tab` case: the caller's own declared pool of tab positions and their alignment kinds, read in declaration order (§3.6.1's own 'it is necessary to identify tab positions, tab types... and the characters to be set') — `jlreq_line::tab_line`'s own `stops` argument. Required of a `tab` case; absent or ignored for any other kind.

tab_stop.description: One declared tab position and its alignment kind — `jlreq_line::TabStop` and `jlreq_line::TabKind` in the case format's own spelling (§3.6.2's four kinds). There is deliberately no nested object for `TabKind::Character`'s own `at`: the same flattening `jlreq-conform/src/kumihan.rs`'s own `case_space_of` already gives `jlreq_spacing::Reduction::Range`'s `floor`/`stage` — a `kind` string plus a sibling field present only for the variant that reads it, rather than a second shape per kind.

position.description: Where this stop sits, in the caller's own unit.

kind.description: `start`, `end` and `centered` align the run's own start, end or center to `position`; `character` aligns the start of the item `at` names instead, and is the only one of the four `at` applies to.

at.description: Which occurrence `kind: "character"` names: an item ordinal into the base stream itself, the same one `items` indexes — not an offset from the target run's own start — `jlreq_line::TabKind::Character`'s own `at`, which `tab_line` refuses unless it falls inside the target run's own item range. Present only for `kind: "character"`, absent for the other three the way `space.floor` is absent outside a reducible `space`.

stream.description: One annotation stream: the same shape as the base one, validated by the same routine, indexed by its own ordinal (ADR 0016, ADR 0018).

scale.description: One declared character size, in the caller's own unit. Anisotropic on purpose: §3.3.3 gives one-third ruby (三分ルビ) a block extent of half the base em and an inline extent of a third, so a single scalar per size cannot hold it.

item.description: One occurrence of one Appendix A key (ADR 0018). `conform --check` requires every item to be exactly one key — except a Western ligature, which is several cl-27 keys on the proportional frame — because a case whose input kumihan would refuse to build a `Text` from tests nothing.

start.description: Where this occurrence begins, in bytes of its own stream. Strictly increasing, on a character boundary, in range.

advance.description: How wide the caller measured it, in their own unit. Supplied rather than computed: kumihan never asks how wide a character is (ADR 0002).

scale.description: Which of the stream's declared sizes this occurrence is set at.

frame.description: What the supplied advance covers: the character frame (字幅). Required whenever Appendix A names the item's key under cl-01, cl-02, cl-05, cl-06 or cl-07, and `conform --check` enforces it — there the frame decides a geometry and an unstated one has no answer to report (ADR 0018). It is also the axis that separates two Appendix A listings of one code point, which is the single fact a foreign implementation needs to answer any §A.1 or §A.27 case: §A.27 marks its 778 rows `proportionally-spaced` and §3.1.2 states the advance of §A.1's brackets as half-width, so `U+0028` declared on the half em is cl-01 and the same key declared proportional is cl-27. A frame is not only a geometry here; it is evidence about the occurrence, and an implementation that classifies from the code point alone cannot answer either case.

role.description: The syntactic job the document gives this occurrence, which selects the class whose Appendix A section is about that job: `decimal-point` and `digit-group-separator` reach §A.24, the characters of a grouped numeral (連数字); `unit-symbol` reaches §A.25; `quantity-symbol` reaches cl-27 through §C.2 note 11; `sentence-terminator` reaches §A.6 and §A.7; and `sentence-medial` reaches §A.4, which §3.1.6 is about. Appendix A names a job in a Remarks cell for four rows only — §A.24's `U+0020`, `U+002C` and `U+002E` and §A.25's `U+0020`, and three of the four state it in the Japanese half alone — so for every other key the role is the caller stating what their document means rather than a lookup.

candidate.description: One break opportunity, at a byte offset into the base stream.

constructs.description: The constructs declared over the streams above. A construct is named in a report by its kind and its position in its array — the ruby you wrote third — never by an identity kumihan allocated, because a caller never saw those (ADR 0015). Every kind but `feasible`, `lower` and `place` either declines outright whenever a case declares one of these at all, or declines per item wherever one covers it (`crates/jlreq-conform/src/kumihan.rs`'s own module doc); `feasible`, `lower` and `place` are the three kinds this object is load-bearing for, and not all in the same way. `feasible` reads `constructs` alongside an otherwise-ordinary base stream, question and candidates: `jlreq_line::Feasible::compute` takes a `jlreq_unit::Runs` overlay directly and a `feasible` case's own adapter method builds one from exactly this object rather than refusing on its account, but the case is still fundamentally about a break candidate, with `constructs` supplying the overlay that lets kinsoku's own same-run refusal see it. `lower` and `place` are each the object's own kind of question in a way `feasible` is not: neither asks anything about a break candidate, a boundary or a composed line at all. `lower` asks only what `jlreq_inline::lower` resolved for one declared `ruby` construct — every field a `lower` case's own `expect.lower` states is a fact about the construct this object declares, and none of them is reachable through any other field of `input` (`$defs/expect`'s own `lower` description states the shape). `place` asks what `jlreq_inline::place` computes once `lower`'s own resolution is read and consumed — every attachment `expect.place` states is a fact about where one of `constructs.ruby`'s own annotation characters actually lands, positioned against a line layout this format derives from the declared items rather than accepting as a further field (`$defs/input`'s own `kind` description states why).

range.description: A half-open range of ordinals into one stream, as `[first, past-the-end]`. The runner rejects a case that indexes one stream with another's ordinal, which is the same invariant `ItemIndex` and `AnnotationIndex` hold inside kumihan (ADR 0016).

ruby.description: One ruby construct: a range of the base stream, the annotation stream holding the reading, and the run pairing. There is deliberately no size here and no `ruby.size` policy question — the annotation stream's own `scales` is where the ruby em is stated, and it is stated once (ADR 0019).

run.description: One pairing inside a ruby construct: which base characters this reading belongs to. §B.2 notes 9 through 11 and §C.2 notes 6 through 8 all turn on whether two neighbors are in the same run, which is why the pairing is data rather than an inference.

emphasis.description: One emphasis-dot (圏点) construct. No stream and no side, because §3.3.9 fixes the size and the side and repeats one mark.

symbol.description: The mark, as a hexadecimal code point.

permitted.description: One permitted answer, with the policy that selects it and the source that states it.

policy.description: An overlay on `Policy::JLREQ`: a partial map from a question's stable dotted path to a choice's stable name. `{}` names none, so it applies to every policy and is the case's fallback entry. Renaming a question therefore breaks the case files at gate time rather than silently. Both halves of the pair are published data rather than Rust: `spec/derived/questions.tsv` records every question path with the answers the specification permits it, quoted from the sentence that permits them, and `conform --check` refuses a path that file does not carry and a choice name it does not list.

source.description: Who states this answer: "JLReq preferred (B.2#2)", "JIS X 4051 (3.1.9, Figure 77)", and so on.

forbidden.description: One outcome the specification excludes, and the sentence that excludes it.

expect.description: What an implementation should answer. A `forbidden` entry states only the fields it forbids, so every field here is optional and a missing one asserts nothing.

violations.description: Every rule the composition could not satisfy, by address. An empty array asserts that it satisfied all of them.

class.description: A classification answer: the class number §3.9.2 gives, and the rules that decided it.

boundary.description: A boundary answer. The conditional spaces, never their sum: §B.2 note 3 makes the space between two middle dots the sum of a quarter em of each, and §D.2 note 1 then gives the two components different reduction priorities, which a single number cannot state (ADR 0014).

before.description: The item ordinal on the one real side of the boundary. For an interior boundary (`edge` absent) this is the item immediately preceding it, matching `jlreq_spacing::Adjacency::between`'s own `before` parameter. At the line end (`edge: "end"`) it is still the immediately preceding item — the one `Adjacency::at_line_end` builds the boundary from. At the line head (`edge: "head"`) there is no preceding item, so this instead names the one item the boundary precedes, matching `Adjacency::at_line_head`'s own `first` parameter: a line edge always has exactly one real neighbor, and `before` always names it, whichever side it is on.

edge.description: Which line edge this boundary sits at, when it is not an interior adjacency between two items: `head` for the boundary before the line's first item (Table 1 through 6's line-head row), `end` for the boundary after its last item (their line-end column). Absent for an ordinary interior boundary between `before` and the item after it. Without this field a rule whose only citation is a line-edge cell — Table 3's `(before: 5, after: line-edge)` cell among them — was unreachable by any case: every `before` was read as naming an interior boundary alone, and the line-end boundary `jlreq_spacing::Adjacency::at_line_end` answers is a different adjacency, not a `before` this integer, by itself, had any way to name.

expansion.description: The boundary's own Table 6 opportunity, independent of `spaces`: ADR 0014's amendment (ADR 0021) moves this off the conditional space entirely, because Table 6 states one opportunity per class pair, a fact about this coordinate, not about either neighbor's own contribution — the identical move ADR 0014 already made for `ruby_overhang` above. Present, and meaningful, even where `spaces` is empty: cl-19 against cl-19 (kanji beside kanji) is `blank` in Table 1 (no conditional space of either referent's) but `0-1/4 stage 3` in Table 6, and this field is what makes that coordinate's own expansion opportunity assertable at all — before this field existed, a boundary with no conditional space had no way to publish an expansion answer, and `jlreq_spacing::evaluate::spaces_of`'s own per-term loop could not read Table 6 for a coordinate with no term to iterate over regardless of what Table 6 stated there.

rules.description: Every rule the answer's own boundary-level citations must include, by address — a subset of `CaseBoundary::rules`, never their equality and never their order. `check_boundary` reads this field as "every address named here must appear somewhere among the answered rules," not as a demand that an implementation reproduce `jlreq_spacing::evaluate::rules_fired`'s own fixed-slot array in that array's own internal order, or without that array's own repeated fallback addresses — reproducing kumihan's own chain of citations is exactly the demand ADR 0006 exists to keep the suite from making of an engine that merely answers the boundary question. A declared address met by an implementation that publishes no rules at all — an empty `CaseBoundary::rules` — is passed over rather than failed, the identical third state `boundary_expansion.rule` above already gives its own one citation. This is what makes `rules: ["B.2#17"]` at a line-head boundary before cl-01 a real, checked assertion for the first time (`docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s `3.1.5` and `B.2#17` entries), and what makes `B.2#13`'s own placement citation at cl-26's line-head and line-end boundaries assertable too — though not `D.2#4`'s own citation at the identical two coordinates, which lives only in a reduction table's per-term loop that never runs where Table 1 states no term to reduce, so no comparison surface reaches it regardless of this field. Before this field had a reader, the schema already parsed it and no case's declaration was ever checked against an answer at all (twelve pre-existing declarations, in `A.16.json` and `A.22.json`, none of them live against this workspace's own answers because every one sits on a ruby-construct-covered boundary — `jlreq-inline` is built now, but `boundary`'s own adapter method still declines outright over any item a declared construct covers, exactly as `feasible`'s own arrival did not change it either: `constructs` is `feasible`'s and `lower`'s own load-bearing field, never `boundary`'s, because neither `jlreq_spacing::Adjacency`'s own `class_of` nor the boundary evaluator it feeds carries a construct overlay through, and building one for it is no part of this round or of M4-a round 1's own scope — `crates/jlreq-conform/src/kumihan.rs`'s own module doc states the reason once for every kind it applies to).

boundary_expansion.description: One boundary's own expansion opportunity — `jlreq_spacing::Expansion`, read from `jlreq_spacing::Boundary::expansion` rather than from any one conditional space.

kind.description: `none` (no opportunity here), `range` (expandable to a stated ceiling at a stated stage), or `residual` (§3.8.4 step (d): no upper limit, filled only once every other expandable site is exhausted).

ceiling.description: The highest this boundary may be expanded to. Present only for `kind: "range"`; `resolved` is absent, because a boundary-level opportunity has no single referent's size to resolve it against the way a `space`'s own amount does.

stage.description: The priority stage this opportunity expands at (§E.1's own four steps; stage 1, the Western word space, is outside Table 6 and never appears here). Present only for `kind: "range"`.

feasible.description: One break candidate's own survival through kinsoku — `jlreq_line::Feasible::compute`'s answer for a single entry of `input.candidates`, anchored the way `boundary` anchors on one `before` (`check_question` in `xtask/src/conform.rs` holds a `feasible` case to naming the same candidate throughout, the identical invariant it already holds `classify` and `boundary` to). `candidate` is the ordinal *into `input.candidates`*, not a byte offset and not an item ordinal: the format already spells three different coordinate systems in nearby fields — a byte offset in `candidates[].at`, an item ordinal in `boundary.before` and `class.item` — and a reader who assumed one of those here would ask about the wrong array entirely. `breakable` states whether kinsoku left the candidate standing in `Feasible::breaks()` (`true`) or refused it into `Feasible::rejected()` (`false`); `rules` is the subset comparison `boundary.rules` already uses — every address named here must appear somewhere among the answer's own citations for this one candidate, never their equality and never their order (`crates/jlreq-conform/src/run.rs`'s own `check_rules` states the reasoning this field reuses unchanged). `jlreq_line::Feasible::compute` silently passes a candidate over — reports it in neither `breaks()` nor `rejected()` — when its own byte offset names no item boundary the stream's own segmentation carries; this shape carries no third field for that state, because an implementation that reaches it answers the whole case `None` (not attempted) rather than inventing a value here for a fact the evaluator never decided (`Compose::feasible`'s own doc states this choice and why it was made rather than the alternative of a three-valued field).

candidate.description: The ordinal into `input.candidates` this expectation is about — the position in the array the case itself declares, matching `boundary.before`'s own "named by the case, not by kumihan" reading rather than any coordinate kumihan computes.

breakable.description: Whether kinsoku left this candidate standing (`true`, in `Feasible::breaks()`) or refused it (`false`, in `Feasible::rejected()`).

rules.description: Every rule the answer's own citation for this candidate must include, by address — a subset of the answer's own published rules, compared the way `boundary.rules` already is.

lower.description: One declared ruby construct's own `jlreq_inline::lower` answer — every field a fact `lower` resolved for it, none reachable through `boundary`, `feasible` or a composed line. `construct` is the ordinal into `input.constructs.ruby` this expectation is about, the identical 'named by the case, not by kumihan' reading `boundary.before` and `feasible.candidate` already give their own subject; `check_question` in `xtask/src/conform.rs` holds a `lower` case to naming the same construct throughout, the invariant it already holds `classify`, `boundary` and `feasible` to. Every other field is optional and a missing one asserts nothing, `feasible`'s own convention made uniform here. `same_run` and `separations` are read from the construct's own `Contribution::runs` and `Contribution::separations` — §B.2 notes 9 through 11 and §C.2 notes 6 through 8 turn on the first, §3.3.8 rule 1 on the second — while `alignment` and `alignment_discouraged` are read from `Contribution::alignment_of` and `Contribution::alignment_discouraged`, real for `RubyStyle::MonoRuby` and `RubyStyle::JukugoRuby` alike — §3.3.7¶1 delegates a jukugo compound's own ≤2-character runs to "the method described in § 3.3.5" without qualification, so `lower` resolves the identical fact for it — and `None`/`false` for `RubyStyle::GroupRuby`, the one style §3.3.5 never governs. `rules` is the subset comparison `boundary.rules` and `feasible.rules` already use — every address named here must appear somewhere among the answer's own citations for this construct, never their equality and never their order (`crates/jlreq-conform/src/run.rs`'s own `check_rules` states the reasoning every one of the three reuses unchanged). There is deliberately no field here for a per-construct alignment override: ADR-0019's per-construct-beats-policy precedence is this workspace's own bookkeeping about which of two doors an alignment came through, not something JLReq states, so a conformance case asserting it would measure kumihan's own API rather than the specification; it is covered by unit tests in `crates/jlreq-inline/src/lower.rs` instead, and a `lower` case selects between the two alignments through `permitted[].policy`'s own `ruby.alignment` overlay exactly as every other policy-conditioned reading in this format is selected.

construct.description: The ordinal into `input.constructs.ruby` this expectation is about — the position in the array the case itself declares, matching `boundary.before`'s and `feasible.candidate`'s own 'named by the case, not by kumihan' reading.

same_run.description: Whether two items of the base stream share a run, per `jlreq_unit::Runs` — the exact predicate §B.2 notes 9 through 11 and §C.2 notes 6 through 8 all turn on. Every entry names its own pair; two entries are never merged or compared against each other.

separations.description: The complete list of forced boundary spacing `Contribution::separations` reports across every construct the case declares, not only the one `construct` names — a total list compared by count and by position the way `boundary.spaces` already is, so a case stating one entry asserts both that it exists and that nothing else does. `least` is a bare unit count in the case's own caller unit, never a `$defs/amount` fraction: unlike Table 1's own terms, the amount §3.3.8 rule 1's forced separation carries is not a fraction of an em JLReq states anywhere — it is the caller's own reading measured wider than its own base, split by `docs/decisions/mono-ruby-separation-split.md`'s own reading — so publishing it as a fraction would assert a JLReq amount that does not exist to assert. Omitting `least` from an entry asserts only that a separation exists at `after`, nothing about its amount.

alignment.description: The `RubyAlignment` `Contribution::alignment_of` resolved for `construct` — `nakatsuki` (中付き) or `katatsuki` (肩付き), §3.3.5's own two methods. Real for `RubyStyle::MonoRuby` and `RubyStyle::JukugoRuby` alike, on §3.3.7¶1's own wholesale delegation to §3.3.5's method; a case naming a `group` construct here asks a question `lower` never resolves one for, because §3.3.6 states no nakatsuki/katatsuki choice at all.

alignment_discouraged.description: Whether the alignment above is §3.3.5's own discouraged combination — katatsuki resolved in horizontal writing, which the section says 'should not be adopted' without forbidding it (ADR-0011). `Contribution::alignment_discouraged`'s own answer: `lower` honors the resolution regardless of this flag, never refusing it, so a case asserting `true` here must also assert `alignment: "katatsuki"` for the assertion to be the discouraged combination and not a contradiction. Real for a `RubyStyle::JukugoRuby` construct exactly as it is for `RubyStyle::MonoRuby`, on the settled reading that §3.3.7¶1's own wholesale delegation to 'the method described in § 3.3.5' carries the recommendation with it, not only the arithmetic — a genuinely open question §3.3.7 itself leaves unstated, argued in full in `Contribution::alignment_discouraged`'s own doc.

rules.description: Every rule the answer's own citation for this construct must include, by address — a subset of the answer's own published rules, compared the way `boundary.rules` and `feasible.rules` already are.

same_run.description: One same-run assertion: whether two items of the base stream, named by ordinal, share a `jlreq_unit::RunId`. An object rather than a bare `[i, j, bool]` triple, matching this format's own established practice — `run`, `tab_stop` and `candidate` are all objects, and `range` is the sole bare array this schema publishes, for a pairing with no third field to carry.

items.description: The two item ordinals compared, into the base stream.

same.description: Whether the two items share a run.

lower_separation.description: One forced boundary spacing `lower` computed, in the case's own caller unit rather than through `$defs/amount` (`$defs/lower`'s own `separations` description states why).

after.description: The item this boundary follows — `jlreq_unit::Separation::after`, the identical 'the item immediately preceding the boundary' reading `boundary.before` already gives an interior adjacency.

least.description: The forced amount, in the case's own caller unit. Absent asserts only that the boundary carries a forced separation, nothing about its amount.

place.description: What `jlreq_inline::place` computed for one caller-declared `Constructs`: every annotation it placed, in the order `place` walked the declared ruby — mono-ruby's own, group-ruby's own and a jukugo compound's own alike, under either of §3.3.7's own two paragraphs — and every run it declined to place, for one of `Attachments::declined`'s own four stated reasons: a mono-ruby run's own katatsuki-with-overflow choice, §3.3.5(c)'s own, unresolved for want of a `Question` (task #81), reachable through a jukugo paragraph-1 run too; a group-ruby run whose ruby is genuinely longer than its base, §3.3.6 paragraph 3's own half, whose two stated methods both spread the base characters apart rather than moving the ruby, which `jlreq_inline::place` cannot perform, reachable through a jukugo paragraph-2 compound answering `Question::JUKUGO_RUBY_LAYOUT`'s own `group` too (`decision:jukugo-group-layout-distribution`); a jukugo compound answering `phonetic`, §F's own distribution being unimplemented; or a jukugo compound whose base range one `place` call's own line only partially covers — never a different absence than one of those four. `declined` names each such run by the ordinal of the declared `constructs.ruby` entry it belongs to, the identical position `lower.construct` already names an entry by. There is deliberately no `rules` field here: [`jlreq_inline::place::Attachments`] publishes no `rules_fired` of its own, because §3.3.5, §3.3.6 and §3.3.7 are each one rule address and `lower` already records the first the moment it resolves an alignment (`crates/jlreq-inline/src/place.rs`'s own module doc) — a second accessor answering the identical question is exactly what ADR-0019 forbids, so a `rules` field here would invite a case to assert a citation this kind never publishes. A reader who finds this field's absence surprising should read it as this paragraph's own deliberate omission, not as an oversight this format left to be filled in later.

attachments.description: Every annotation `place` placed, in `Attachments::attachments`'s own walk order.

declined.description: The declared `constructs.ruby` ordinal of every run `place` declined — a mono-ruby run reaching §3.3.5(c)'s own katatsuki-with-overflow branch, a group-ruby run reaching §3.3.6 paragraph 3's own ruby-longer-than-base branch, a jukugo compound answering `phonetic`, or a jukugo compound whose base range one `place` call only partially covers, alike (this property's own parent `place` description states all four in full) — `Attachments::declined`, translated through `ConstructRef::ordinal`. Asserting the specific ordinal, and not merely that the list is non-empty, is the point: 'nothing was placed' is satisfiable by an implementation that never placed anything at all, while naming the construct is satisfiable only by one that reached one of those four reasons and declined there.

attachment.description: One placed annotation character — `jlreq_inline::place::Attachment`, narrowed to the two facts these cases turn on. `size`, `side`, `run` and `construct` are all real accessors `Attachment` carries but none is stated here: `size` and `run` are untested by every case this kind's own cases publish today, and `side` answers `Side::BlockStart` structurally for every attachment this milestone's `place` produces (`crates/jlreq-inline/src/place.rs`'s own module doc) — an accessor that always answers the same constant is not coverage, and stating it here would invite a reader to mistake its presence for §3.3.4 being measured, which stays deferred (`docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s own §3.3.4 entry).

inline.description: This attachment's own inline-axis origin, in the case's own caller unit and in the derived line's own coordinates (`$defs/input`'s own `kind` description states how that line is derived) — `Attachment::inline`, a bare unit count rather than a `$defs/amount` fraction, because a placement is a caller-unit coordinate rather than a fraction of an em JLReq states anywhere. May be negative: a run centered under nakatsuki that is genuinely wider than its own base starts before it (`InlineExtent::sub_sat`'s own signed difference).

item.description: The annotation stream's own item ordinal this attachment draws — `Attachment::item`, `None` only for a construct that repeats one member rather than placing a stream (emphasis dots, unimplemented this round).

space.description: One conditional space: one neighbor's contribution to the space at a boundary. Carries no expansion of its own (ADR 0014, amended by ADR 0021): see `boundary.expansion` for Table 6's own opportunity at this same coordinate.

referent.description: Whose em the amount is a fraction of, which Appendix B writes `be` and `af`.

reduction.description: How the amount shrinks. §3.1.9's two-valued case is not a range: it says twice that at the line end "the possibilities are only half em spacing or solid", and a continuous notion of shrink emits the value the specification forbids.

ladder.description: Which ladder the stage below belongs to. Appendix D's six steps and Appendix E's four are two orderings of two different things and §3.8.2 orders the ladders themselves, so a bare stage would mean two things in one field (ADR 0014) — the reason the disambiguator exists, though a `space` can now only ever name `reduction` here: Appendix E's own stage lives on `boundary.expansion.stage` instead, since ADR 0021 moved the opportunity that stage numbers off this object entirely.

line.description: One composed line. The three quantities are ADR 0017's and none is reconstructed by the runner, because two runners would reconstruct them differently.

placements.description: The caller's own glyph-box origins, always on the line's own inline axis and relative to the line's origin, one per item of the line. May be negative and may run past `extent`. A segment's interior items are here like any other; §3.2.5's tate-chu-yoko (縦中横) does not run along this axis, so its items all carry the segment's own inline origin and their spread is `parts[].across`.

trailing.description: The realized conditional space at the line end, whether or not it lives inside the last item's supplied advance.

extent.description: The line in normalized geometry, excluding anything hung outside the measure.

trims.description: Every unit taken out of a supplied advance, with the sentence that took it. `conform --check` requires each rule to be §3.1.2 or a Table 1 cell stating that amount with that referent; without the check, an implementation could discharge an overlong line by subtracting an arbitrary quantity from a caller's advance and calling it a trim (ADR 0002, ADR 0017).

parts.description: The sub-lines of every segment touching this line. Empty for a case with no segment, which is most of them.

hanging.description: How far hanging punctuation (ぶら下げ, burasage) extends past the measure.

pull_up.description: §3.1.12 ⑤'s repair as `Search::Optimal` actually applied it to this line — `jlreq_line::PullUp`'s own three fields. **Absent asserts that `Line::pull_up` answers `None` for this line — a positive claim that nothing was pulled up, not the ordinary 'this question goes unchecked' reading every other optional field on this object gets.** That reading is deliberate rather than the more permissive one task #44 (round 16) already had to choose between once, for `ExpectBoundary::rules`, and settled the same way: if absence meant unchecked, every case that does not mention `pull_up` would silently stop constraining it, and this new field would be decorative from the day it is published. It is also the safe reading rather than a retroactively risky one: `Search::FirstFit`'s own doc states `Line::pull_up` is `None`, full stop, on every line that search composes — not because the ladder withholds it but because `FirstFit` never runs the comparison `PullUp` reports the outcome of — so every one of the 466 cases published before this field existed already answers `None` here regardless of whether its own author ever considered the question, and turning the assertion on retroactively changes what none of them are measured against. Present only under `Search::Optimal`, and then only on a line where a nearer candidate break was genuinely evaluated and the search still took a farther one, closing the gap with real reduction (`PullUp`'s own doc; `pull_up_of`'s two conditions, `crates/jlreq-line/src/compose.rs`).

§3.1.12 ⑤'s repair, as `jlreq_line::PullUp` reports it for one line: a nearer candidate break existed and was scanned, and the search took a farther one instead, reduction reclaiming the room that took — the specification's own 'ideally... the character... would be moved onto the first line' (§3.1.12 ④), read where reduction actually succeeds rather than where the worked figure states it does not.

amount.description: How much this line's own reduction reclaimed to admit the farther choice, in the caller's own unit — `PullUp::amount`, the realized reduction summed across every site `Adjustment::reduced` names for this line, not a single Table 1 or Appendix D term of its own, so it is stated as a plain length rather than through `$defs/amount`'s fraction.

pulls.description: Which item of the base stream moved up onto this line as a result — `PullUp::pulls`, an ordinal into `items` the same way `trim.item` and `class.item` are: the boundary the nearer, un-taken candidate would have ended this line at, which is where the next line would otherwise have started.

rule.description: The rule that states the repair — `PullUp::rule`, always §3.1.12 from this workspace's own implementation (`pull_up_of`'s own literal `RuleId::EXAMPLES_OF_LINE_ADJUSTMENT`). Compared conditionally, on `boundary.expansion.rule`'s own semantics directly above: a declared address met by a decliner's silence is passed over rather than failed, so an implementation that reports a pull-up without publishing a specification address for it stays measurable by `amount` and `pulls` alone.

trim.description: One unit count taken out of one item's supplied advance, with the sentence that took it.

part.description: One sub-line of one segment. `inline` and `block` are its origin relative to the line's; `across` is one block offset per interior item and is non-empty only for §3.2.5's tate-chu-yoko (縦中横).

disagreement.description: One implementation kumihan has measured that answers this case differently. Publishing these is uncomfortable and correct: a case saying "we read §3.1.9 this way, this implementation does otherwise, here is why" is more useful to the ecosystem than a green suite that hides the question (ADR 0006).

evidence.description: Where kumihan's reading is recorded, as a repository path.
